title: ProjectE executable verification matrix report
description: Output of tools/scripts/assert_matrix.py. The verification matrix already mapped every rule to a level, a tool, a loop and an action on failure - as prose, which is only as live as the last person who read it. This artifact is that mapping evaluated. It contains no measurement of its own: every assertion binds a claim to a LOCATION in a report some other tool produced, so the tool stays the single source of the measurement and this layer is the single source of the claim about it.

status.description: RED > NO_COVERAGE > SCREEN_ONLY > GREEN. SCREEN_ONLY is not a new concept: the matrix already uses it in section 5 for tools whose output cannot be hash-bound. It ranks below NO_COVERAGE because not knowing is a stronger statement of ignorance than knowing without a binding.

measures_nothing.description: Pinned true. Re-deriving an engineering quantity here would give the repo two answers to one question, which is what item #51 (one rule, three copies, two numbers) and #54 (two independent implementations) were both about.

rule.description: Copied verbatim from the matrix row. Matching is exact on normalised text and never fuzzy: a fuzzy match would re-point the assertion at a neighbouring row the moment somebody rewords one, and a rule silently checking the wrong thing is what this layer exists to prevent.

level.description: The matrix taxonomy, which decides what a PASS may claim. A/B must carry an executable predicate; one that does not is UNBACKED_CLAIM, meaning the matrix says the rule is file-measurable and nothing measures it.

on_fail.description: The matrix's fifth column, finally read by a machine. A finding nobody knows how to act on is a finding that does not get acted on.

operator.description: A closed set. There is no expression escape hatch, because a rule that cannot be diffed cannot be reviewed.

selector.description: Dotted keys and numeric indices only. No wildcards: a wildcard reads as one assertion but covers a set whose size depends on the report, and the empty set compares vacuously true.

tolerance.description: Required for every magnitude comparison and may be 0 - the point is that a boundary policy was chosen rather than inherited from float arithmetic. (0.7-0.4)/2 is 0.1499999... and a 0.15 threshold has twice turned exactly-on-the-limit items into violations in this repo.

units_selector.description: Mandatory whenever units is declared. A tool's unit label can lie and no reader here can catch that; what this catches is an unlabelled number being compared against a labelled threshold.

falsifier.description: The mutation that must flip this assertion to FAIL. Mandatory for every executable assertion: the matrix's own acceptance criteria refuse to call a checker live without positive AND negative fault injection.

syntax_errors.description: Assertions that would not load. Collected rather than raised, so one malformed rule does not hide the state of the others - but still RED, because a rule that does not load is a rule nothing enforces. Every refusal happens at LOAD time: an assertion that only blows up when its evidence happens to be present is silently unenforced on every run where it is absent.

reason.description: PATH_ABSENT, STALE_EVIDENCE, EVIDENCE_MISSING, UNIT_MISMATCH, UNITS_UNDECLARED, TYPE_MISMATCH, MEASUREMENT_ABSENT, RECORD_INCOMPLETE. A selector that finds nothing is PATH_ABSENT and therefore NO_COVERAGE - never FAIL and never PASS, because a field that is not in the report means the tool did not measure it, and comparing null is how 0 == 0 once got reported as agreement.

margin.description: observed minus threshold, so an on-the-boundary comparison is visible instead of silent.

evidence_bound.description: False when the report carries no declared digest tying it to the artifact it measured. Not fatal, not free: a run whose passes all rest on unbound evidence is SCREEN_ONLY.

on_fail.description: Present only on FAIL. Carried through from the matrix row so the report says what to do, not just what broke.

proofs.description: Result of --prove: the declared fault injected into a copy of the evidence, requiring the assertion to catch it. Still passing is VACUOUS_ASSERTION - decoration rather than a check. Dropping to NO_COVERAGE is FALSIFIER_NO_COVERAGE: the injected fault destroyed the measurement instead of being caught by it, which is a quieter kind of useless and is what a 'remove' falsifier always produces.

establishes.description: PASS counted by what it establishes. A run that is green on four filings and two measurements must not read like one that is green on six measurements, and a single PASS count makes those identical. The matrix calls dressing a level C document gate up as a level A measurement the most dangerous error in this repo: the line that reads 'checked' and measured nothing.

matrix_coverage.description: Present when --matrix was given. The matrix stays the single source and is READ, never transcribed into a second file - transcription is how one rule became three copies with two different numbers. An unasserted rule is absence of coverage, not a violation; an orphan assertion IS a defect, because it passes forever and reads as coverage while enforcing nothing.

parse_problems.description: A table listing rules with no level column is reported here rather than skipped: the matrix's own first sentence is that a rule without a level is not a rule.
